children: According to CNBC, the White House on Friday evening announced plans to claw back $810 million in congressionally appropriated funding, drawing criticism from lawmakers. The move would block $567 million for Health and Human Services programs for refugees, asylees and other non-citizens, $28 million for HHS research, and additional funding for the Education Department's special programs for immigrant students. The White House cited the Impoundment Control Act as the basis for its authority, while the Government Accountability Office has said the law does not allow withholding proposed rescissions through expiration if Congress has not approved them. Sen. Susan Collins, who chairs the Senate appropriations committee, called the move an attempt to undermine Congress's power of the purse and said pocket rescissions are unlawful.

title: White House Seeks To Claw Back $810 Million In Congressionally Appropriated Funding
